Additional_Background:
Software Architecture feels formulaic and interpretative at the same time. The canonical solutions exist for a reason but applying them to a real life porblem more than often require some level of improvisation. Because of this, I wouldn't be confortable saying I have extensive experience level in any of the topics even though I've tackled high performance challenges in highly critical systems. (maybe analysis)
e.g.: Solving throughput issues in PIX payment pipelines for a high profile brazilian bank to enhance user experience by reducing latency in operations. The overall solution was a producer/consumer approach (formulaic and I'd say a really basic pattern), but the moving pieces, the workarounds and adaptation to the bank's ecosystem required some kind of freestyle. Constraints that are rarely seen or anticipated in a whiteboard session for example.
